---
title: "Flipper Length by Species (R)"
author: "Sarika Tasnim"
date: "2026-09-23"
---

Data: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/),
Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

In this post I compare flipper length across penguin species.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
```

First, I remove rows with missing values.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data
#| tbl-cap: "The original dataset"
penguins_clean <- penguins |> na.omit()
head(penguins_clean)
```

Next, I summarise flipper length for each species.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flipper
#| tbl-cap: "Flipper length (mm) by species."
penguins_clean |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    mean_flipper = mean(flipper_length_mm),
    min_flipper = min(flipper_length_mm),
    max_flipper = max(flipper_length_mm),
    count = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_flipper)) |>
  kable(digits = 1)
```

Finally, I compare flipper length across species with a boxplot.

```{r}
#| label: fig-flipper-species
#| fig-cap: "Flipper length by species."
ggplot(penguins_clean, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Flipper length (mm)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Gentoo penguins have the longest flippers, while Adelie penguins
have the shortest.
